newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen rebounds to end firmer on stock fall.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen rebounds to end firmer on stock fall.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures rebounded from morning lows to close firmer on Monday after falling for four business days.

An afternoon plunge in the Tokyo stock market triggered quick buy-backs in the December contract, traders said. Tokyo stocks were sold following a media report that Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka suggested that the consumption tax could be raised again in the future after a scheduled rise on April 1.
The December ended up 0.04 at 98.94. It briefly fell to 98.81, the lowest level for any benchmark contract since July 31, 1996. Turnover was 135,288 contracts.
The key contract dropped sharply in the morning in line with rises in cash interest rates across the yield curve after the Bank of Japan's neutral operation, traders said.
Against what the market had expected of an injection of 200 billion yen or more, the BOJ supplied 100 billion yen on Monday morning in the face of a market shortfall of 90 billion yen.
This resulted in a jump of the key overnight call rate to 0.58 percent. Friday's weighted average was 0.53 percent.

"The December was sold on disappointment over the neutral operation," said a long-term credit bank dealer. "We had expected the BOJ to try to keep the key overnight rate from rising sharply at least until March 31."
If the key December falls further to 98.75, that suggests the market has factored in a rise in the BOJ's discount rate to 1.0 percent from the current 0.5 percent, traders said.

A city bank dealer said: "It seems to me that today's neutral operation was suggesting that we should be prepared for a rise in interest rates, which may not come in March or April, but some time in the near future."
Another bank dealer said that the BOJ's operation may have been aimed at finding out whether fund suppliers will buy long-term certificates of deposits (CD) when market rates rise.
But no bids were detected in one-, two- or three-month CDs. Key three-month CDs were offered at 0.56 percent, against last issued rate of 0.58 percent, traders said.

"Because the BOJ confirmed that investors were not willing to buy the CDs even with higher rates, the bank may conduct an accommodative operation from tomorrow to help ease banks' fund raising demand before the book closings," he said.
